quote: ‘But he hasn’t got anything on,’ a little child said.
source: Hans Christian Andersen, The Emperor’s New Clothes, at the procession near the close (trans. Jean Hersholt, 1949)

evidence.where: The Hans Christian Andersen Centre at the University of Southern Denmark hosts Jean Hersholt's translation in full. The sentence reads: “But he hasn't got anything on,” a little child said. The next sentences run: “Did you ever hear such innocent prattle?” said its father, and the tale then gives “But he hasn't got anything on!” the whole town cried out at last. The proposal's wording matches Hersholt exactly, including the comma inside the speech and the closing full stop.
evidence.edition: The Complete Andersen, trans. Jean Hersholt (The Limited Editions Club, New York, 1949); tale first published in Eventyr, fortalte for Boern, 1837
evidence.locator: The procession, at the moment the child speaks, a few lines before the whole town takes up the cry
